answers.Set Your Scope: I am Operations Manager for a 40-branch retail bank in Botswana, responsible for branch back-office processing (account opening, KYC refresh, loan document checks). Sector: retail banking.
answers.Map Opportunity One: Use document AI to pre-check KYC refresh packs before they reach the central team. Cost of inaction: about 1,900 packs a month are rejected for missing documents, roughly 950 staff hours and BWP 180,000 a year in rework. Nobody has acted because KYC sits between Compliance and Operations and neither wants to own a model that touches regulated files.
answers.Map Opportunity Two: For the Credit team, an AI assistant that drafts the first credit memo from the loan application. Cost of inaction: memo drafting averages 3.5 hours per SME loan, about 600 loans a year, delaying decisions by four days. Nobody has acted because the Head of Credit fears auditors will question AI-written memos.
answers.Map Opportunity Three: Stretch, outside my remit: Marketing could use branch transaction patterns to predict which SME customers are about to leave. Cost of inaction: we lost 210 SME accounts last year, about BWP 2.1m in deposits. Nobody has acted because Marketing has no data access agreement with Operations.
answers.Choose the One You Would Stake Your Repu: Opportunity One. I own the back-office process end to end and the rework cost is already in my budget line, so I can run a pilot in five branches without anyone else's approval. The Compliance concern is real, so the pilot keeps a human checker on every flagged pack.
answers.AI pressure-test and AI Lens: I asked an AI assistant to list overlooked automation opportunities in branch back-office work; it surfaced the credit memo idea I had not considered. I used it to sanity-check the BWP 180,000 estimate, which it put lower until I added the overtime rate. It could not tell me why Compliance resists ownership: that political read is mine, from two steering meetings this year.

results.feedback: This is an exceptional submission that meets all the criteria for a strong answer. You have provided highly specific opportunities with concrete financial and operational costs of inaction (e.g., the BWP 180,000 rework cost and the BWP 2.1m deposit loss). Your political analysis of why these opportunities have not been pursued—citing auditor fear, data access agreements, and ownership vacuums—shows a sophisticated understanding of organizational dynamics. The choice to stake your reputation on Opportunity One is well-reasoned, focusing on your direct control and a pragmatic approach to risk management. Your reflection on the AI lens clearly distinguishes between the 'calculating' power of AI and the 'political' judgment of the transformation leader.

This is an exemplary submission that perfectly balances quantitative data with political intuition. You have provided concrete costs for inaction (e.g., the BWP 180,000 rework cost and the 2.1m deposit loss) and named specific barriers such as the lack of a data access agreement and audit fears. Your choice of Opportunity One is well-reasoned, leveraging your own budget authority and direct control to bypass political deadlock. The AI pressure-test section effectively demonstrates how AI can serve as a sanity check for estimates while acknowledging that it cannot replace the nuanced political reading required to navigate a banking hierarchy.

Excellent submission that sets a high standard for the Opportunity Map. You provided concrete, verifiable metrics (such as the BWP 180,000 rework cost and the 210 SME accounts lost) and a sophisticated understanding of the internal politics preventing progress, such as the ownership gap between Compliance and Ops and the fear of audit regarding AI-written memos. Your AI lens reflection is particularly strong, demonstrating how AI can refine quantitative estimates while highlighting the human expertise required to navigate corporate culture and regulatory friction. Choosing the opportunity you own end-to-end demonstrates a pragmatic leadership mindset.
